_comment: Tokens that end in a period WITHOUT ending a sentence. Consumed by extension/src/core/segment.js and desktop/src/executive_reader/textproc/segment.py.
notes: A single capital letter followed by a period is an initial, not a sentence end. Handle in code, not here.
A period followed by a digit is a decimal. Handle in code.
Ellipses are one token and do not end a sentence unless followed by a capital.
Dr appears in both titles and geographic on purpose: Doctor and Drive. Consumers union all categories, so the duplicate is inert.
_list_markers: A token of digits only, or a single letter, followed by a period, at the very START of the text being segmented, is a list marker and never ends a sentence. Both halves segment one block or line at a time, so position zero is where '1. ' always sits and nowhere else. Without it every numbered list is spoken as 'one.' pause 'First item', which is the shape of the defect rather than a detail of it: the pause lands between the number and the thing it numbers. The single-letter half covers 'a. ' and 'b. '. The extension's initials rule only ever matched a CAPITAL letter, because it was written for 'J. R. R. Tolkien', so a lowercase marker was not already handled there; anchoring it at the start is safer than widening the initials rule, which would also stop splitting a sentence genuinely ending in a lone letter. KNOWN LIMIT, recorded rather than discovered later: 'Step 1. Preheat the oven' still splits, because the digit is not at the start. That is the price of a rule that can never fire mid-sentence, and it is the right price.
